lines: 第一章：量子归零
剧痛是有颜色的。
在彻底失去意识的前一秒，黄海涛看到的是刺眼的白，那是实验室高能粒子对撞机防护罩破裂时泄露的切伦科夫辐射光；紧接着是令人窒息的黑，那是失控的油罐车撞碎挡风玻璃带来的死亡阴影。
这两种极端的色彩在他濒死的脑海里疯狂搅拌，最后坍缩成一个奇点。
不知过了多久，也许是一秒，也许是亿万年。
第一感觉是触觉。
他感到全身的重量都在被抽离，仿佛每一个细胞都被一只无形的大手狠狠撕扯、拉伸，又重新捏合。这种感觉不像肉体受伤，更像是一种底层的、构成“自我”的信息流正在被强制解码，再通过某种无法理解的协议重新编码。
一声干涩的**从他喉咙里挤出。他猛地睁开眼，剧烈的咳嗽让他蜷缩起来。
空气清冷，带着一种从未呼吸过的凛冽。没有汽油味，没有血腥味，也没有医院icu里令人烦躁的消毒水味。取而代之的，是一股极其复杂的高浓度气息——腐烂的阔叶植物散发出的腐殖质甜香、某种辛辣的姜科植物根茎被踩碎后的辛味、还有高空中游离臭氧被雷暴电离后的独特金属腥气。
这是纯氧的味道。不，比纯氧更复杂，是氧气含量极高但又混合了无数种挥发性有机化合物的原始大气。
黄海涛艰难地撑起身子，手掌按在潮湿的地面上。泥土松软得惊人，指尖陷进去的触感不像现代板结的田园土，而是一种充满弹性的、饱含水分的海绵状物质。他低头看去，土壤是深红褐色的，上面覆盖着一层厚厚的、由巨大叶片和黑色藤蔓构成的腐殖层。
他强迫自己冷静下来，目光扫过四周。
“这是……哪里？”
他喃喃自语。面前是一片望不到边际的原始丛林。树木高大得违反常理，那些在现代被称为“擎天树”的巨木在这里只是中等个头。一棵需要十几人合抱的巨树拔地而起，树皮上覆盖着一层滑腻的青苔和发光的苔藓。更诡异的是，那些在现代属于草本或灌木的植物，在这里都进化成了乔木形态——巨大的观音座莲蕨（angiopterisevecta）长得像椰子树一样高，宽大的叶片像巨大的羽毛，在微风中发出类似丝绸摩擦的沙沙声。
空气中飞舞着肉眼可见的巨型飞蚁，翅膀在透过树冠缝隙射下的光束中反射出彩虹般的光泽。一只体长超过半米的幽灵螳螂正倒挂在藤蔓上，它的镰刀前肢保持着捕食姿态，腹部呈现出一种完美的透明状，甚至能看到里面正在消化的绿色液体。
“黄……黄海涛？”
声音从右后方传来，虚弱，但带着一丝急切。
黄海涛猛地回神，顾不上身体的剧痛，踉跄着绕过一丛长满尖锐倒刺的紫色灌木。在几米开外，李元茜正靠在一块布满奇特纹路的灰色岩石上，大口喘息。
她的样子比他好不到哪去。标志性的黑框眼镜只剩下一条镜腿，另一只镜片碎裂成蛛网状；身上那件印着“中科院古生物所”logo的白大褂已经被荆棘撕扯得不成样子，露出的手臂上划满了细密的血痕。但她还活着，而且手里依然死死攥着那个防水防震的红色采样箱——那是她的命根子。
“元茜！你怎么样？”黄海涛冲过去，本能地想要扶住她，却又怕碰到她的伤口。
“别碰我……没事，只是擦伤。”李元茜摆摆手，声音有些颤抖，但眼神已经开始恢复那种科研工作者的锐利，“告诉我这不是濒死幻觉。我们刚才不是在g65高速，长张高速段吗？那辆刹车失灵的重型罐车……”
她的话戛然而止，因为她也闻到了这空气中独特的味道。
黄海涛深吸一口气，强迫自己进入工作状态。他是地理学家，也是一名野外生存爱好者。他迅速检查了一下自己的装备：阿玛尼西装已经成了破布，但内衬口袋里的一支钢笔式多功能工具还在；手腕上的百达翡丽表盘碎裂，指针死死卡在14:28——车祸发生的时间。
“车祸发生了。”黄海涛的声音低沉而冷静，这是他在野外遇到突发状况时的本能防御机制，“但我们没死。或者说，我们的意识没死。”
他抬起头，看向那片被巨大蕨类植物遮蔽的天空。“看植被。这是典型的热带-亚热带季风性常绿阔叶林，但物种密度和个体体积完全不对。在现代，这种生态结构只存在于亚马逊或者刚果盆地的无人区核心，而且绝不可能有这么高纬度的巨型植物。”
李元茜已经蹲下身，戴上一只备用的简易护目镜，从采样箱里抽出一把不锈钢地质锤。她敲下一小块脚下的岩石，放在手心里掂量。
“你看这个。”她递给黄海涛一块指甲盖大小的石头。
黄海涛接过，在指尖摩挲。这是一块紫红色砂岩，质地疏松，里面夹杂着大量的长石和石英颗粒，还有一些细小的、尚未完全玉化的木质碎片。
“这是古河道沉积岩。”黄海涛的眉头紧锁，“看这交错层理的纹理，水流方向是自西北向东南，流速极快，每秒至少两米以上，是典型的洪流搬运特征。但这周围的植被显示这里已经很久没有发生过大规模洪水冲刷了。”
“这说明什么？”

Chapter 1: Quantum Return to Zero
1.
Severe pain has color.
The second before he completely lost consciousness, what Huang Haitao saw was dazzling white, which was the Cherenkov radiation leaked when the protective cover of the laboratory's high-energy particle collider ruptured; followed by suffocating black, which was the shadow of death caused by the out-of-control tanker smashing the windshield.
These two extreme colors stirred wildly in his dying mind, and finally collapsed into a singularity.
I don’t know how long it took, maybe a second, maybe hundreds of millions of years.
The first sense is touch.
He felt that the weight of his whole body was being pulled away, as if every cell was being torn apart, stretched, and kneaded again by an invisible hand. This feeling does not feel like a physical injury, but more like an underlying flow of information that constitutes the "self" is being forcibly decoded and then re-encoded through some incomprehensible protocol.
"Uh..."
A dry sound was squeezed out of his throat. He opened his eyes suddenly and curled up with a violent cough.
The air was cold, with a chilliness that had never been breathed before. There is no smell of gasoline, no smell of blood, and no annoying smell of disinfectant in the hospital ICU. Instead, there was an extremely complex and high-concentration smell - the sweet smell of humus exuded by rotting broad-leaf plants, the pungent smell of some spicy ginger plant roots that had been trampled, and the unique metallic smell of free ozone in the high air that was ionized by thunderstorms.
This is the smell of pure oxygen. No, it is more complicated than pure oxygen. It is a primitive atmosphere with extremely high oxygen content but mixed with countless volatile organic compounds.
Huang Haitao pushed himself up with difficulty and pressed his palms on the wet ground. The soil is surprisingly soft, and when your fingertips sink into it, it doesn't feel like modern hardened pastoral soil, but a spongy substance that is full of elasticity and full of moisture. He looked down and saw that the soil was dark reddish brown, covered with a thick layer of humus made of huge leaves and black vines.
He forced himself to calm down and glanced around.
"Where...is this?"
he muttered. In front of us is an endless primitive jungle. The trees are unnaturally tall, and those giant trees known in modern times as "Supertrees" are only average in size here. A huge tree that needs a dozen people to hug rises from the ground, and the bark is covered with a layer of slippery moss and glowing moss. What’s even weirder is that plants that are considered herbs or shrubs in modern times have evolved into arbor forms here – the giant angiopterisevecta grows as tall as a coconut tree, with broad leaves like huge feathers, making a rustling sound like silk friction in the breeze.
Giant flying ants visible to the naked eye were flying in the air, their wings reflecting a rainbow of light in the light beams that shot through the gaps in the tree canopy. A ghost mantis with a body length of more than half a meter is hanging upside down on a vine. Its scythe forelimbs maintain a predatory posture, and its abdomen is perfectly transparent, and you can even see the green liquid being digested inside.
"Huang...Huang Haitao?"
The voice came from the rear right, weak, but with a hint of urgency.
Huang Haitao suddenly came back to his senses, ignoring the severe pain in his body, and staggered around a purple bush covered with sharp barbs. A few meters away, Li Yuanqian was leaning on a gray rock covered with strange lines, breathing heavily.
She looked no better than he did. Only one temple leg of the iconic black-rimmed glasses was left, and the other lens was shattered into a spider web shape; the white coat with the "Institute of Paleontology, Chinese Academy of Sciences" logo printed on it had been torn into disarray by thorns, and the exposed arms were covered with fine blood marks. But she is still alive, and she is still clutching the waterproof and shockproof red sampling box in her hand - it is her lifeblood.
"Yuan Qian! How are you?" Huang Haitao rushed over, instinctively wanting to support her, but he was afraid of touching her wounds.
"Don't touch me...it's okay, it's just a scratch." Li Yuanqian waved her hands, her voice was trembling, but her eyes had begun to regain the sharpness of a scientific researcher, "Tell me this is not a near-death hallucination. Weren't we just on the G65 Expressway, Changzhang Expressway? That heavy tank truck with failed brakes..."
Her words stopped abruptly because she also smelled the unique smell in the air.
Huang Haitao took a deep breath and forced himself into working mode. He is a geographer and a wilderness survival enthusiast. He quickly checked his equipment: the Armani suit was in tatters, but the pen-like multi-tool in the lining pocket was still there; the Patek Philippe dial on his wrist was shattered, and the hands were stuck at 14:28 - the time of the car accident.
"A car accident happened." Huang Haitao's voice was low and calm, which was his instinctive defense mechanism when encountering unexpected situations in the wild. "But we are not dead. In other words, our consciousness is not dead."
He raised his head and looked at the sky covered by huge ferns. "Look at the vegetation. This is a typical tropical-subtropical monsoon evergreen broad-leaved forest, but the species density and individual size are completely wrong. In modern times, this kind of ecological structure only exists in the core of no-man's land in the Amazon or the Congo Basin, and there is absolutely no way there are giant plants at such high latitudes."
Li Yuanqian knelt down, put on a spare pair of simple goggles, and pulled out a stainless steel geological hammer from the sampling box. She knocked a small piece of rock off her feet and weighed it in her hands.
"Look at this." She handed Huang Haitao a stone the size of a fingernail.
Huang Haitao took it and rubbed it on his fingertips. This is a purple-red sandstone with a loose texture, mixed with a large number of feldspar and quartz particles, as well as some small wooden fragments that have not yet been completely jade.
